differences.justification: This is the weakest cut because it lies on the gold corridor and loses a quiet tonal contrast, but the one-way Latin Quarter extension requires an island capacity cut. Final enjoyment review must not assume its material survived.
This removes an adjacent micro-stop from an already dense Notre-Dame cluster and frees narration capacity; it is a content consolidation, not a walking-distance improvement.

This is a meaningful archaeological content loss rather than a geometric win. It is acceptable only as a capacity trade for the requested broader outdoor route and remains a final enjoyment-review risk.

differences.item: Square Jean XXIII before Notre-Dame Cathedral
differences.justification: The gold order supports an east-end finish. This route visits the east garden before turning west through the Cathedral toward the Left Bank, avoiding a later east-west return after Notre-Dame. The measured 329m leg makes the local reversal explicit.

differences.item: Memorial des Martyrs de la Deportation
differences.justification: The Memorial is the gold tour's far-east finale. Keeping it before a Sorbonne finish would push east and then require a substantial west-south return. Its powerful ending is a real experiential loss, but this is the strongest endpoint-driven geographic cut.
The 339m routed leg carries the walker from Notre-Dame onto the Left Bank toward the endpoint. Its 42-second source capacity makes it a brief bridge rather than a competing finale.
The Sorbonne supplies a substantial 262-second endpoint stop and a coherent Latin Quarter destination. Its 729m and 14:49 final leg is the principal final-playback risk to review after authoring.
